message.content: {"summary":"You wrote a competent case report with a clear no-ship conclusion and a balanced for/against discussion. Your introduction and recommendation are strengths. To improve, add the missing abstract and visuals, correct the Volkswagen case, complete your references, and build a decision framework explaining when known-defect products may ship and how accepting the contract fits with not shipping.","next_steps":["Add a ~150-word abstract and at least one relevant figure or table, such as a stakeholder impact matrix or a decision flowchart, to support your no-ship argument.","Correct the Volkswagen case in 'The Most Ethical Path' to diesel emissions cheating, complete all reference details, and add reputable sources for each major claim.","In 'DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship' and 'RECOMMENDATION', add a decision framework for shipping known-defect products, evaluate large-scale testing, and reconcile accepting the contract with delaying/not shipping, including disclosure implications."],"criteria":{"C1":"You meet Excellent: your introduction clearly frames Rachel’s dilemma, links it to engineering design and organisational competition, and lists stakeholders. To consolidate this level, deepen how each stakeholder’s interests conflict—especially the chip supplier, health department and emergency services—and keep the explicit design-context link.","C2":"You present balanced for/against arguments (competition, revenue, jobs, harm, codes, reputation) and conclude not to ship. To reach Excellent, give decision-making recommendations for several stakeholders, not just Rachel/company, and reconcile accepting the contract with delaying/not shipping, including contractual and disclosure implications.","C3":"Your report is logically ordered from for/against arguments to a supported no-ship conclusion. To reach Excellent, make the stakeholder analysis systematic for all parties—chip supplier, health department, emergency services—and explicitly link each argument to the conclusion. A decision framework would strengthen the chain of reasoning.","C4":"You use Apple, NHS and Volkswagen cases plus a 1% of 5,000 servers calculation. To reach Very good, correct the Volkswagen description (the cited article concerns diesel emissions cheating, not electric vehicles/crash-safety tests), complete citation details, and add more reputable references and qualitative/quantitative evidence for each major claim.","C5":"You include the required sections except the abstract, and writing is mostly fluent. To reach Good, add a ~150-word abstract, correct typos such as 'DICUSSION', 'of could', 'ofprofessional', 'Actin' and 'ofcompetence', add at least one relevant figure/table, and fix inconsistent/incomplete references (e.g., [3] lacks a URL)."}}
